description: The relics of the first Christian martyr were brought from Jerusalem to Constantinople in the fifth century, and the Church celebrates his courage and forgiveness.

name: Saints Isaac, Dalmatus and Faustus
description: Three Syrian monks of Constantinople: Isaac was the confessor of Emperor Valens, Dalmatus his disciple, and Faustus Dalmatus' son. They defended the faith of Nicaea.

name: The Seven Youths of Ephesus
description: Seven young Christians who hid in a cave during the persecution of Decius and, according to tradition, slept for centuries before waking to a Christian city. A sign of the resurrection.
patronOf: Young men, those who hope in the resurrection

name: Martyr Eusignius of Antioch
description: A veteran of the army of Constantine who was martyred in 362 for rebuking Julian the Apostate for his apostasy.

name: Martyr Dometius the Persian
description: A Persian who converted to Christianity, became a monk and died during Julian's reign for refusing to cease his works of charity and his preaching.
patronOf: Converts, those who help the poor

name: Venerable Emilian the Confessor of Cyzicus
description: Bishop and confessor under the iconoclast emperor Leo the Isaurian, who is remembered for his steadfastness.

name: Martyr Euplus of Catania
description: A deacon of Catania in Sicily, martyred around 304 for holding the Gospel book in the face of the governor.
patronOf: Deacons, those who guard the Scriptures

name: Martyrs Photius and Anicetus
description: Nephews of the martyr Anicetus of Nicomedia, who were put to death under Diocletian for refusing to give up their faith.
patronOf: Young people, those who stand for faith

name: Saint Maximus the Confessor
description: Byzantine monk and theologian (c. 580-662) who defended the true human will of Christ against Monothelitism and had his tongue and right hand cut off. He is a father of Orthodox theology.

name: The Holy Prophet Micah
description: The prophet of Moresheth who foretold that the ruler of Israel would come forth from Bethlehem and who summed up the law in 'do justice, love mercy, walk humbly with your God'.
patronOf: Those who seek justice and mercy

name: The Transfer of the Holy Image Not Made by Hands
description: The Church remembers the arrival in Constantinople in 944 of the Mandylion, the cloth bearing the face of Christ, said to have been sent to King Abgar of Edessa.

name: Martyr Myron of Cyzicus
description: A priest of Cyzicus and a loved shepherd who was martyred around 250 for refusing to offer sacrifice to the emperor.

name: Martyrs Florus and Laurus
description: Twin brothers, stonemasons from Illyria, who built a church and were put to death in the second century. They are patrons of horses and of stonemasons.

name: Martyr Andrew the General
description: A Roman general in Asia Minor martyred around 300 with 2,593 soldiers for refusing to abandon Christ. His faith moved his men to join him.

name: The Holy Prophet Samuel
description: The last judge of Israel, called as a boy to serve in the temple. He anointed Saul and David as kings and is a model of listening: 'Speak, Lord, for your servant hears'.
patronOf: Those called by God, young people

name: The Holy Apostle Thaddeus of the Seventy
description: One of the Seventy who, according to tradition, preached in Edessa and healed the king Abgar. He is honoured with the early evangelisation of the East.

name: Martyr Agathonicus of Nicomedia
description: A man of Nicomedia martyred with companions in the third century for confessing Christ. His name means 'victorious in goodness'.

name: Martyr Lupus of Thessalonica
description: The servant of Saint Demetrius who took the saint's bloodied robe and was martyred around 306. The Church honours his bold faith.
patronOf: Servants, those who follow the saints

name: The Holy Apostle Titus of the Seventy
description: Convert and companion of Saint Paul who served as first bishop of Crete. The letter to Titus gives counsel for the care of the Church.

name: Martyrs Adrian and Natalia
description: A Roman officer and his wife who, inspired by the courage of Christian martyrs, converted and died for the faith in Nicomedia around 304. Natalia cared for the imprisoned.
patronOf: Married couples, those who help the persecuted

name: Venerable Poemen the Great
description: Egyptian desert father of the fifth century whose name means 'shepherd'. Many of the most-loved sayings of the Desert Fathers are his, on patience and humility.

name: Saints Alexander, John and Paul the New of Constantinople
description: Three patriarchs of Constantinople honoured together. Alexander opposed Arius at Nicaea, John IV was a man of prayer and humility, and Paul the New was a defender of icons.

name: The Deposition of the Belt of the Theotokos
description: In the fifth century the belt of the Virgin Mary was placed in the church of Chalkoprateia in Constantinople, honoured for its healing graces.

name: Saint John the Faster
description: Patriarch of Constantinople (d. 595) who lived with austerity and took the title 'ecumenical' as a servant of unity. His name recalls his love of fasting.

name: Hieromartyr Babylas of Antioch
description: Bishop of Antioch martyred under Decius around 250, who refused to let the emperor enter the church because of his guilt. Saint John Chrysostom preached on him.

name: The Holy Prophet Zechariah
description: The prophet who spoke of the king coming on a donkey and of a fountain opened for sin and uncleanness. He is honoured as one who encouraged the exiles returning to Jerusalem.
patronOf: The returned exiles, those who hope

name: The Miracle of the Archangel Michael at Colossae
description: A feast recalling the archangel's deliverance of a church at Colossae from a flood, through a spring that was blessed and healed many.
patronOf: Those who seek the archangel's protection

name: Martyr Sozon of Cilicia
description: A shepherd boy of Cilicia who destroyed a pagan idol and was martyred around 304. He is honoured as a patron of shepherds.

name: The Righteous Joachim and Anna
description: The parents of the Virgin Mary, who prayed for a child in their old age. The Church honours them as the grandparents of Christ and patrons of families.

name: Martyrs Menodora, Metrodora and Nymphodora
description: Three sisters of Bithynia who lived as ascetics and were tortured and martyred around 306 for their faith.

name: Venerable Theodora of Alexandria
description: A married woman of Alexandria who repented of an act of unfaithfulness, lived disguised as a monk in a monastery for years, and was honoured for her long penance.

name: Martyr Autonomus of Bithynia
description: A bishop who fled persecution in Italy to Bithynia, built a church and was martyred around 313 while praying at the altar.

name: Great Martyr Nicetas the Goth
description: A Gothic prince converted by Bishop Ulfilas who was martyred in 372, burned for his faith by the pagan king Athanaric.
patronOf: Goths, those who stand for faith

name: Martyrs Sophia and Her Daughters Faith, Hope and Love
description: A Roman widow named Sophia ('wisdom') and her three daughters, whose names mean the theological virtues. They were martyred in the second century under Hadrian.

name: Venerable Eumenius of Gortyna
description: Bishop of Gortyna in Crete (d. 7th century), known for his holiness and for working wonders. He is honoured as an exemplar of pastoral care.

name: Martyrs Trophimus, Sabbatius and Dorymedon
description: Three Christians of Antioch in Pisidia martyred in 276 for confessing Christ, after enduring imprisonment and torture.

name: Great Martyr Eustathius Placidas
description: Roman general who was converted by a vision of a stag bearing a cross. He lost everything, was restored by God and was martyred with his wife and sons under Hadrian.
patronOf: Hunters, those who suffer loss, families

name: The Conception of Saint John the Baptist
description: The Church celebrates the announcement to Zechariah by the angel Gabriel, six months before the Annunciation to Mary, that Elizabeth would conceive John the Forerunner.
patronOf: Parents who hope for a child, those who prepare the way

name: Martyr Callistratus and His Companions
description: A Roman soldier of Carthage martyred around 300 with forty-nine companions, converted by his witness. He was thrown into the sea in a sack.

name: The Holy Apostle Ananias of the Seventy
description: The disciple of Damascus who baptised Saul after his vision on the road, calling him 'brother Saul'. He is the model of welcoming a former enemy in Christ.

name: Hieromartyr Cyprian and Martyr Justina
description: A magician of Antioch who tried to lure the virgin Justina with spells, was converted by her steadfastness and became bishop; both were martyred around 304.

name: Hieromartyr Hierotheus of Athens
description: First bishop of Athens, tradition holds, a disciple of Saint Paul and teacher of Saint Dionysius the Areopagite.

name: Martyr Charitina of Amisos
description: A young Christian woman of Amisos on the Black Sea martyred in 304 after enduring tortures with patience and prayer.
patronOf: Young women, those who endure suffering

name: The Holy Apostle Thomas
description: The apostle who doubted the resurrection until he saw Christ, then confessed 'my Lord and my God'. Tradition holds that he brought the Gospel to India.

name: Great Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus
description: Two Roman officers beloved by the emperor Maximian, who were tortured and killed in Syria around 303 for refusing to worship idols. They were united in friendship and faith.

name: The Holy Apostle James, Son of Alphaeus
description: One of the twelve apostles, said to have preached in Judea and Egypt and to have been martyred in Ostrakine. He is sometimes called James the Less.

name: Martyrs Eulampius and Eulampia
description: A brother and sister of Nicomedia martyred around 303 under Diocletian after boldly confessing Christ in the city.

name: The Holy Apostle Philip the Deacon
description: One of the Seven chosen to serve the widows at Jerusalem, who proclaimed Christ in Samaria and baptised the Ethiopian eunuch. His four daughters were prophetesses.

name: Martyrs Probus, Tarachus and Andronicus
description: Three Christians of Cilicia who were arrested during the persecution of Diocletian and martyred at Tarsus around 304 after boldly confessing the faith.

name: Martyrs Nazarius, Gervasius, Protasius and Celsus
description: Early martyrs of Milan, discovered by Saint Ambrose in 386 and honoured in Italy and across the Church. Their relics healed the sick and confirmed the faith.

name: Venerable Euthymius the New
description: Monk of Thessalonica and Mount Athos (c. 823-898) who lived in great ascetic labour as a disciple of Elder Joseph and was honoured as a model of monastic devotion.

name: Martyr Longinus the Centurion
description: The Roman soldier at the cross who, seeing the signs at Christ's death, confessed 'truly this was the Son of God'. Tradition says he later became a Christian and was martyred in Cappadocia.

name: The Holy Prophet Joel
description: The prophet who foretold the outpouring of the Spirit on all flesh, which Peter proclaimed at Pentecost. The Church reads his call to repentance and hope.

name: Great Martyr Artemius
description: A Roman general under Constantine who was martyred in 362 under Julian the Apostate for rebuking the emperor for apostasy. He is invoked for the healing of stomach pain.

name: Saint Abercius, Equal to the Apostles
description: Bishop of Hieropolis in Phrygia (d. c. 167) who travelled to Rome and was honoured for his preaching and healings. His epitaph is one of the oldest Christian inscriptions.

name: The Holy Apostle James, Brother of the Lord
description: First bishop of Jerusalem, called 'the Just', who presided at the Council of Jerusalem and was martyred around 62. The Divine Liturgy of Saint James is attributed to him.

name: Great Martyr Arethas and Companions
description: Leader of the Christian community of Najran in Arabia who was martyred in 523 with 4,299 others by a Himyarite king who forced them to renounce Christ.

name: Martyrs Marcian and Martyrius of Constantinople
description: Two notaries of the Church of Constantinople in the fourth century who served the patriarch. They were martyred for refusing to deny Christ.

name: Great Martyr Demetrius the Myrrh-Streamer
description: Roman official and beloved patron of Thessalonica, martyred around 306. His tomb is said to have flowed with fragrant oil that healed pilgrims.

name: Martyrs Terence and Neonilla
description: A mother and her children martyred in Syria in the third century after confessing Christ. The Orthodox Church honours them as a family of martyrs.

name: Martyrs Zenobius and Zenobia
description: A bishop of Aegae in Cilicia and his sister, physicians who healed the poor without payment and were martyred around 285.

name: The Holy Apostles Stachys, Amplias, Urban and Companions
description: Disciples of Saint Paul greeted in the letter to the Romans. Stachys, 'my beloved', became the first bishop of Byzantium.

name: Martyrs Acindynus, Pegasius, Aphthonius, Elpidephorus and Anempodistus
description: Five Persian Christians martyred under Shapur II in the fourth century, who refused to renounce Christ and were killed in a series of tortures.

name: Martyr Acepsimas the Bishop
description: Bishop of Hnaita in Persia, aged eighty, martyred in 376 with his priest and deacon in the persecution of Shapur II.

name: Venerable Joannicius the Great
description: Bithynian hermit (754-846) who lived as a shepherd, soldier and hermit and spent his life in service to God. He was honoured as a wonderworker and peacemaker.

name: Saint Paul the Confessor of Constantinople
description: Patriarch of Constantinople in the fourth century, exiled several times for defending the faith of Nicaea against the Arians, and martyred around 350.

name: The Thirty-Three Martyrs of Melitene
description: A group of Roman soldiers of Melitene martyred around 300 for refusing to renounce Christ, led by Hieron and Nicander.

name: The Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the Bodiless Powers
description: The Church honours Michael, leader of the heavenly hosts, together with all the angels who serve God. It is one of the most important feasts of the angels.

name: The Holy Apostles Erastus, Olympas, Rodion, Sosipater, Quartus and Tertius
description: Companions of Saint Paul greeted in the letter to the Romans. Erastus served the city of Corinth as treasurer and later became a bishop.

name: Saint John the Merciful, Patriarch of Alexandria
description: Patriarch of Alexandria (c. 550-616) who gave all the Church's wealth to the poor, calling them 'my masters'. He fed thousands during a famine.

name: Saint John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople
description: Archbishop (c. 347-407), 'golden-mouthed' for his preaching, who defended the poor and was exiled twice by the imperial court. His Divine Liturgy is the most used in the Orthodox Church.

name: Martyrs Gurias, Samonas and Abibus
description: Three martyrs of Edessa, put to death under Diocletian in the early fourth century. They are invoked as protectors of marriage, and the Church tells of their healing of a faithless wife.

name: The Holy Apostle and Evangelist Matthew
description: The tax collector called by Christ, who left his table to follow him and wrote the first Gospel. He preached in Ethiopia according to tradition.
patronOf: Tax collectors, bankers, those who change their lives

name: Saint Gregory the Wonderworker
description: Bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus (c. 213-270), pupil of Origen. He converted nearly the whole city, which had only seventeen Christians when he arrived.

name: Martyr Plato of Ancyra
description: A young man of Ancyra, martyred in 306 after encouraging his fellow Christians and being tortured for confessing Christ.

name: The Holy Prophet Obadiah
description: The prophet who spoke against Edom and, according to tradition, hid and fed a hundred prophets in caves in the time of Ahab and Jezebel.

name: Venerable Gregory of Decapolis
description: Monk (c. 780-842) who travelled across the Byzantine world and the Balkans, teaching the faith and defending icons against iconoclasm.

name: Saint Amphilochius of Iconium
description: Bishop of Iconium (c. 340-395), cousin of Saint Gregory the Theologian and companion of Saint Basil. He was a defender of the Trinity and of the Holy Spirit's divinity.

name: Venerable Alypius the Stylite
description: Paphlagonian saint (c. 522-640) who lived on a pillar for 53 years after a lifetime of service to the poor, and was known for his wisdom and care of his people.

name: Martyr James the Persian
description: A Persian official who denied Christ under pressure from the king, repented and was tortured and cut limb by limb in 421. The Church honours his repentance.

name: Martyr Stephen the New
description: Byzantine monk (c. 715-767) who defended holy icons under Constantine V and was martyred. His life shows the cost of fidelity.

name: Martyr Paramon and 370 Martyrs
description: A group of 370 Christians martyred with Paramon in Bithynia in 250 under Decius for refusing to deny Christ.

name: The Holy Prophet Nahum
description: Prophet of the seventh century BC who foretold the fall of Nineveh and proclaimed good news on the mountains: 'the Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble'.

name: The Holy Prophet Habakkuk
description: The prophet who asked God why evil prospers and learned that 'the righteous shall live by faith'. His book ends in a hymn of joy in the Lord.

name: The Holy Prophet Zephaniah
description: A prophet of the seventh century BC who warned of the 'day of the Lord' and promised that God would rejoice over his people with singing.
patronOf: Those who seek the Lord in humility

name: Venerable Patapius of Thebes
description: Egyptian hermit (d. c. 650) who left Thebes to live in Constantinople and was known for healing, hospitality and constant prayer.

name: The Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos by Righteous Anna
description: The Church celebrates the conception of the Virgin Mary by Joachim and Anna, nine months before her nativity. It honours God's care in preparing the Mother of the Lord.
patronOf: Mothers who hope for a child, Mary's devotees

name: Martyrs Menas, Hermogenes and Eugraphus
description: Three Christians of Alexandria martyred around 313 under Maximin. Menas was an Egyptian merchant and Hermogenes was a scribe.

name: Venerable Daniel the Stylite
description: Syrian monk (409-493) who lived on a pillar near Constantinople for 33 years and was known for his counsel to the emperors and care of the poor.

name: Saint Spyridon the Wonderworker
description: Bishop of Trimythous in Cyprus (c. 270-348), a shepherd who attended the Council of Nicaea. His relics are honoured on Corfu, and he is widely loved for his care of the poor.

name: Martyrs Thyrsus, Leucius and Callinicus
description: Three martyrs of Bithynia killed under Decius in the third century, who endured torture while praising Christ.

name: Hieromartyr Eleutherius of Illyria
description: Bishop of Illyricum, a young man who became bishop at 20 and was martyred in 126 with his mother Anthia under Hadrian.

name: The Holy Prophet Haggai
description: Prophet of the return from exile who urged the people to rebuild the Temple and promised that the glory of the latter house would be greater than the former.

name: Martyr Sebastian and His Companions
description: A Roman officer who comforted imprisoned Christians and was shot with arrows and then beaten to death around 288 under Diocletian.
patronOf: Athletes, soldiers, those who help the sick

name: Martyr Boniface of Tarsus
description: A Roman official of Tarsus who lived dissolutely, repented and was martyred in 307, after giving his life to the care of the martyrs' bodies.

name: Hieromartyr Ignatius the God-bearer
description: Bishop of Antioch martyred in Rome around 107. On his way to execution he wrote letters to the churches about unity, the Eucharist and the bishop, which remain treasured.

name: Martyr Juliana of Nicomedia
description: A young woman of Nicomedia who refused to marry a pagan official and was martyred around 304 after enduring torture.
patronOf: Young women, those who keep their promises

name: Great Martyr Anastasia the Deliverer from Potions
description: A Roman widow of the fourth century who cared for imprisoned Christians and was martyred under Diocletian. Her name means 'resurrection'.

name: The Ten Martyrs of Crete
description: Ten men of Crete who were beheaded in 250 under Decius for refusing to deny Christ, honoured for their steadfast and joyful faith.

name: The Holy Innocents Slain at Bethlehem
description: The children of Bethlehem killed by Herod's order after Christ's birth. The Orthodox Church honours them as the first martyrs for Christ.

name: Martyr Anysia of Thessalonica
description: A young woman of Thessalonica martyred around 304 when she refused to take part in a pagan sacrifice and was killed by a soldier.

name: Venerable Melania the Roman
description: Wealthy Roman noblewoman (c. 383-439) who gave away her fortune, founded monasteries in Jerusalem and lived a life of prayer and charity.

name: The Circumcision and Name of Jesus
description: Eight days after his birth Jesus was circumcised and given the name Jesus, 'the Lord saves', as the angel had commanded. Lutheran and Anglican churches keep the feast of the Holy Name on New Year's Day.
patronOf: Those who begin the year with Christ's name

name: Elizabeth Ann Seton
description: American widow and mother (1774-1821) who converted to Catholicism, founded the first American religious community and opened the first Catholic parish school. Episcopal and Catholic churches both remember her.

name: George Washington Carver
description: American scientist and teacher (c. 1864-1943), born into slavery, who taught poor farmers to restore soil with crop rotation and peanuts. He gave credit for his discoveries to God, whom he called his guide in the laboratory.

name: The Epiphany of Our Lord
description: The visit of the wise men shows Christ revealed to the nations. Lutheran and Anglican churches keep Epiphany as a principal feast, and many also recall the baptism of Jesus and the wedding at Cana.

name: Jim Elliot and the Ecuador Missionaries
description: On January 8, 1956, five young American missionaries, Jim Elliot, Nate Saint, Ed McCully, Pete Fleming and Roger Youderian, were killed by the Waorani people of Ecuador. Their families later returned and shared the Gospel.

name: Julia Chester Emery
description: American Episcopal leader (1852-1922) who for forty years directed the Woman's Auxiliary to the Board of Missions and helped mobilise the women of the church for mission at home and abroad.

name: William Laud
description: Archbishop of Canterbury (1573-1645) who worked for order and beauty in worship and was executed by Parliament in the English Civil War. He is remembered with respect by many Anglicans.
patronOf: Church order, those who suffer for conviction

name: Aelred of Rievaulx
description: English Cistercian abbot (1110-1167) who wrote 'Spiritual Friendship', teaching that friendship in Christ is a way to know God. He governed 600 monks with gentleness.
patronOf: Friends, abbots, those who seek community

name: Hilary of Poitiers
description: Bishop of Poitiers (c. 310-367) who defended the full divinity of Christ at the cost of exile and wrote hymns and commentaries. Lutherans and Anglicans honour him as a teacher of the faith.

name: Eivind Berggrav
description: Norwegian Lutheran bishop (1884-1959) who led the Church's resistance to Nazi occupation, was imprisoned, and wrote on the Church's duty to stand for justice.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
description: American Baptist pastor (1929-1968) who led the civil rights movement through nonviolent action rooted in the Gospel. He was assassinated in Memphis in 1968. Lutheran and Episcopal calendars remember him.

name: Amy Carmichael
description: Irish missionary (1867-1951) who served in India for fifty-five years, rescuing children from temple service and founding the Dohnavur Fellowship. She was a poet and a woman of prayer.

name: Henry of Uppsala
description: English-born bishop of Uppsala (d. 1156) who went with King Eric of Sweden on a mission to Finland and is honoured as the 'apostle of Finland'. He was murdered by a man he had disciplined.

name: Vincent of Saragossa
description: Spanish deacon and martyr (d. 304) who endured torture under Diocletian rather than deny Christ. Lutherans and Anglicans remember him among the early martyrs.

name: Phillips Brooks
description: Episcopal bishop of Massachusetts (1835-1893), one of the great preachers of his age and the writer of the Christmas carol 'O Little Town of Bethlehem'.

name: Timothy, Pastor and Companion of Paul
description: The young pastor of Ephesus, taught the Scriptures from childhood by his mother Eunice and grandmother Lois. Paul called him 'my beloved and faithful child in the Lord'.
patronOf: Young pastors, those who learn from family

name: Lydia, Dorcas and Phoebe
description: Three women who served in the early Church: Lydia, the seller of purple who opened her home to Paul at Philippi; Dorcas, who made garments for the poor of Joppa; and Phoebe, the deacon of Cenchreae who carried Paul's letter to the Romans.
patronOf: Hosts, those who serve in practical ways

name: Thomas Aquinas
description: Dominican friar and teacher (1225-1274) whose Summa Theologiae remains a monument of Christian thought. Lutheran and Anglican calendars honour him as a teacher of the Church.

name: Liliuokalani of Hawaii
description: Last reigning monarch of the Hawaiian Kingdom (1838-1917), a devout Christian, a gifted composer who wrote 'Aloha 'Oe', and a woman of dignity under political loss.
patronOf: Hawaii, musicians, those who lose power

name: Charles I, King and Martyr
description: King of England executed on January 30, 1649, after the Civil War. The Book of Common Prayer once included a service for the day, which many Anglicans still recall.

name: Charles Haddon Spurgeon
description: English Baptist preacher (1834-1892) known as the 'Prince of Preachers', who pastored the Metropolitan Tabernacle in London for decades. He founded orphanages and a pastors' college and died on this day.

name: Anskar of Hamburg
description: Archbishop of Hamburg and Bremen (801-865), the 'apostle of the North', who brought the Gospel to Denmark and Sweden. He is remembered in Lutheran and Anglican calendars.

name: Dietrich Bonhoeffer's Birthday
description: German Lutheran pastor and theologian (born February 4, 1906) who resisted the Nazi regime and wrote 'The Cost of Discipleship'. He was executed in 1945, and his life is remembered on April 9.

name: Agatha of Sicily and the Martyrs of Japan
description: Lutherans and Anglicans remember Agatha, who was martyred in Sicily around 251, and the twenty-six Christians crucified in Nagasaki in 1597.

name: Charles Dickens and the Christmas Carol
description: English novelist (born February 7, 1812) whose books exposed poverty and urged charity. His 'A Christmas Carol' shaped how many people think of generosity at Christmas.
patronOf: Authors, those who work for the poor

name: Bakhita of Sudan, Remembered
description: The Episcopal Church remembers Josephine Bakhita, born in Darfur, enslaved as a child and later a sister and teacher in Italy, who forgave those who had enslaved her.

name: Silas, Companion of Paul
description: Prophet and leader in the early Church who accompanied Paul on his second journey. He sang hymns with Paul in the Philippian jail.

name: Barbara Harris
description: In 1989 Barbara Clementine Harris was consecrated as the first woman bishop in the Anglican Communion. The Episcopal Church recalls her ministry as a priest, bishop and justice advocate.

name: Fanny Crosby
description: American hymn writer (1820-1915), blind from infancy, who wrote more than 8,000 hymns, including 'Blessed Assurance' and 'To God Be the Glory'. She died on this day.

name: Aquila, Priscilla and Apollos
description: The Lutheran calendar remembers the tentmaking couple who taught the eloquent Apollos 'the way of God more accurately', and Apollos who then became a powerful preacher.

name: Philemon and Onesimus
description: Philemon of Colossae, whose runaway slave Onesimus returned with Paul's letter asking him to receive him 'no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother'.

name: Philipp Melanchthon
description: German scholar (1497-1560), Luther's colleague and the principal author of the Augsburg Confession. Called 'Preceptor of Germany' for his work in education.

name: Janani Luwum
description: Anglican archbishop of Uganda (1922-1977) who spoke against the brutality of Idi Amin and was murdered. He is honoured as a modern martyr.
patronOf: Uganda, those who speak for the oppressed

name: Chinese Martyrs Agnes, Agatha and Lucy
description: Three Chinese Catholic women, catechists, who were martyred between 1856 and 1862. The Episcopal Church honours their witness.

name: Frederick Douglass
description: Escaped slave and abolitionist leader (c. 1818-1895) who used Scripture to challenge slavery and championed the rights of women and all people. He died on this day.

name: Eric Liddell
description: Scottish Olympic gold medallist (1902-1945) who refused to run on Sunday, then served as a missionary in China and died in a Japanese internment camp.

name: Margaret of Cortona
description: Italian penitent (1247-1297) who left an unmarried relationship, became a Franciscan tertiary and cared for the poor and sick of Cortona.

name: Matthias, Apostle
description: Chosen by lot to take the place of Judas among the twelve. Lutherans keep his day on February 24, or 25 in a leap year, while other traditions keep it in May.
patronOf: Those who serve faithfully, the overlooked

name: Elizabeth Fedde
description: Norwegian Lutheran deaconess (1850-1921) who founded the first Lutheran deaconess house in America and served immigrants in Brooklyn and Minneapolis.

name: Photini, the Samaritan Woman at the Well
description: The woman Jesus met at Jacob's well, who left her water jar and ran to tell her town that she had met the Christ. The Episcopal Church honours her as an evangelist.

name: Anna Julia Cooper
description: African American educator and scholar (1858-1964), born into slavery, who earned a doctorate in her sixties and taught that education was a path to dignity.

name: John and Charles Wesley
description: Anglican priests and brothers (John, 1703-1791; Charles, 1707-1788) who began the Methodist movement. Charles wrote over six thousand hymns, including 'Hark! The Herald Angels Sing'.

name: John and Charles Wesley, Anglican Commemoration
description: The Episcopal Church remembers the brothers who renewed the Church of England in the eighteenth century through field preaching, small groups and hymns.

name: Elizabeth Barrett Browning
description: English poet (1806-1861) whose faith and love shaped works such as 'Sonnets from the Portuguese'. She wrote against slavery and child labour.

name: Gregory of Nyssa, Bishop and Theologian
description: The Episcopal Church honours Gregory, who defended the Trinity at Constantinople and wrote about the 'perpetual progress' of the soul in God.

name: Harriet Tubman and Sojourner Truth
description: Harriet Tubman (c. 1822-1913) guided more than seventy people out of slavery by the Underground Railroad, guided by prayer. Sojourner Truth (c. 1797-1883) preached freedom and the equality of women.

name: Gregory the Great
description: Bishop of Rome (c. 540-604) who sent Augustine to England, wrote on pastoral care and called himself 'servant of the servants of God'. Lutherans and Anglicans honour him as a model pastor.

name: James Theodore Holly
description: First African American bishop of the Episcopal Church (1829-1911), who moved to Haiti and led the Church there for decades.

name: Vincent de Paul and Louise de Marillac
description: French priest (1581-1660) and widow (1591-1660) who founded the Congregation of the Mission and the Daughters of Charity to serve the poor.
patronOf: Social workers, those who serve the poor

name: Cuthbert of Lindisfarne
description: English monk, bishop and hermit (c. 634-687) who walked among the poor villages of Northumbria preaching and healing.

name: Jonathan Edwards
description: American pastor and theologian (1703-1758), a leader of the Great Awakening, who also served as a missionary to the Mahican people at Stockbridge and became president of Princeton.

name: Gregory the Illuminator
description: The apostle of Armenia (c. 257-331) who converted King Tiridates, established the first Christian state and is honoured as father of the Armenian Church.

name: Oscar Romero
description: Archbishop of San Salvador, shot while celebrating Mass in 1980 after speaking for the poor. Lutherans, Anglicans and Catholics remember him as a modern martyr.

name: Harriet Monsell
description: English Anglican (1811-1883), widow and founder of the Community of Saint John Baptist, an early religious community for women in the Church of England.

name: Charles Henry Brent
description: Episcopal missionary bishop (1862-1929) of the Philippines who worked for the end of the opium trade and for Christian unity, helping to start the Faith and Order movement.

name: James Solomon Russell
description: Episcopal priest (1857-1935) who founded Saint Paul's Normal and Industrial School in Virginia for African American students and led the church in the South.

name: Hans Nielsen Hauge
description: Norwegian lay preacher and reformer (1771-1824) who travelled the country calling for personal faith and founded businesses to help the poor. He was imprisoned for preaching.

name: Mary of Egypt
description: Egyptian penitent of the fifth century who, after a life of sin, lived forty-seven years as a hermit in the desert. Her story is read in many Churches during Lent.

name: John Donne
description: Anglican priest and poet (1572-1631), Dean of Saint Paul's, who wrote 'No man is an island' and the 'Holy Sonnets', including 'Death, be not proud'.

name: Frederick Denison Maurice
description: English Anglican priest and theologian (1805-1872), a founder of Christian socialism who helped create the Working Men's College.

name: James Lloyd Breck
description: Episcopal missionary priest (1818-1876) who founded the mission of Nashotah House and worked in Minnesota and California.

name: Richard of Chichester
description: English bishop (1197-1253) whose prayer 'to see thee more clearly, love thee more dearly, follow thee more nearly' is known across Protestant traditions.
patronOf: Bishops, those who pray for nearness to Christ

name: Martin Luther King Jr., Martyr
description: The Episcopal Church remembers Martin Luther King Jr., killed in Memphis on April 4, 1968, where he stood with sanitation workers.
patronOf: Peacemakers, those who work for justice

name: Harriet Starr Cannon
description: American Episcopal religious (1823-1896), founder of the Community of Saint Mary, the first Episcopal religious order for women.

name: Albrecht Durer, Lucas Cranach and Matthias Grunewald
description: Three great artists of the German Renaissance and Reformation. Durer made woodcuts of the Apocalypse and Passion, Cranach painted Luther's portrait, and Grunewald painted the Isenheim Altarpiece.

name: Tikhon, Patriarch of Moscow
description: Orthodox patriarch (1865-1925) who worked in America and later led the Russian Church through the Revolution, remembered for ecumenical friendship.

name: William Augustus Muhlenberg
description: Episcopal priest (1796-1877) who promoted hymns, schools and the Church's mission to the sick, founding Saint Luke's Hospital in New York.

name: Mikael Agricola
description: Finnish bishop and reformer (c. 1510-1557) who gave Finland its first written language and translated the New Testament into Finnish.

name: George Augustus Selwyn
description: Anglican bishop of New Zealand (1809-1878) who learned Maori and travelled the country on foot to build up the Church among the Maori and settlers.

name: Adoniram Judson
description: American Baptist missionary (1788-1850) who served in Burma for nearly forty years, translated the Bible into Burmese and endured imprisonment and loss.

name: Zenaida, Philonella and Hermione
description: Early unmercenary physicians who cared for the sick without payment: Zenaida and Philonella were sisters of Tarsus, and Hermione was a daughter of the deacon Philip.

name: Corrie ten Boom
description: Dutch watchmaker's daughter (1892-1983) who, with her family, hid Jews from the Nazis. She survived Ravensbruck and spent her later years sharing a message of forgiveness.

name: Peter William Cassey and Annie Besant Cassey
description: An Episcopal deacon (1831-1917) and his wife (1843-1875) who founded the mission church in Cheltenham, leaders of their congregation in Philadelphia.

name: Kateri Tekakwitha
description: Mohawk-Algonquin woman (1656-1680), baptised in 1676, who endured hardship for her faith and became a model of prayer. She is honoured by Anglicans and Catholics.
patronOf: Native Americans, those who face rejection

name: The Diet of Worms
description: On April 18, 1521, Martin Luther stood before the Emperor and refused to recant unless shown his error from Scripture and plain reason. 'Here I stand', he is said to have added.

name: Philipp Melanchthon's Death and Olaus Petri
description: Philipp Melanchthon died on April 19, 1560, and the Swedish reformers Olaus Petri (1493-1552) and his brother Laurentius Petri (1499-1573) are remembered for giving Sweden its Bible and church order.

name: Johannes Bugenhagen
description: German pastor and reformer (1485-1558), Luther's pastor at Wittenberg, who organised the Lutheran church in northern Germany and Denmark.

name: Anselm of Canterbury
description: Archbishop of Canterbury (c. 1033-1109) who wrote 'Cur Deus Homo', defined theology as 'faith seeking understanding' and was a gentle pastor to his monks.

name: Day of Creation
description: The Lutheran calendar marks a day to give thanks for creation and recommit to its care, near Earth Day.

name: Toyohiko Kagawa
description: Japanese Christian (1888-1960), a pastor, labour organiser and author who lived in the slums of Kobe and founded cooperatives and hospitals.

name: Johann Walter
description: German composer (1496-1570), friend of Luther and creator of the first Protestant choir book, who shaped the music of the Reformation.

name: Zita of Tuscany
description: Domestic servant (c. 1218-1272) who served one household in Lucca with great faithfulness and gave generously to the poor.

name: Catherine of Siena
description: Italian mystic and tertiary (1347-1380) who urged the Pope to return to Rome and wrote 'The Dialogue'. Lutherans and Anglicans remember her as a teacher of the Church.

name: Philip and James, Apostles
description: Philip brought Nathanael to Jesus and asked 'show us the Father'; James the Less led the Jerusalem church. Both are remembered on May 1 in Lutheran and Anglican calendars.

name: Athanasius of Alexandria
description: Bishop of Alexandria (c. 296-373) who defended the divinity of Christ at Nicaea and was exiled five times. His letter on the incarnation remains widely read.

name: Elisabeth Cruciger
description: German hymn writer (c. 1500-1535), former nun and friend of Luther, who wrote 'Herr Christ, der einig Gotts Sohn', the first hymn by a woman in the Lutheran tradition.

name: Monica
description: Mother of Augustine of Hippo (332-387), who prayed for her son for years until his conversion. She is remembered by Lutherans and Anglicans for faithful prayer.
patronOf: Mothers, those who pray for children

name: Frederick the Wise
description: Elector of Saxony (1463-1525) who protected Luther after the Diet of Worms and helped the Reformation spread. A prudent ruler and patron of learning.

name: George of Lydda
description: Soldier and martyr (d. c. 304) honoured by many churches, patron of England. Anglicans keep his feast in April and some calendars in May.

name: Carl F. W. Walther
description: German-American Lutheran pastor and theologian (1811-1887), first president of the Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod and author of 'Law and Gospel'.

name: Nicolaus Ludwig von Zinzendorf
description: German count (1700-1760) who welcomed the Moravian refugees to his estate at Herrnhut, sent missionaries across the world and wrote hymns.

name: Johann Arndt and Jacob Boehme
description: Two German spiritual writers who emphasised inner devotion: Arndt (1555-1621), author of 'True Christianity', and Boehme (1575-1624), the shoemaker mystic.

name: Florence Nightingale's Birthday
description: English nurse (born May 12, 1820) who understood her work as a calling from God, founded modern nursing and reformed military hospitals.

name: Frances Perkins
description: American public servant (1880-1965), first woman in a US cabinet, who helped create Social Security and fair labour laws, guided by her Episcopal faith.

name: Pachomius of Tabenissi
description: Egyptian founder of communal monastic life (c. 292-348) who organised monks into communities under a rule of prayer and shared work.

name: Thurgood Marshall
description: American lawyer (1908-1993), first Black Supreme Court justice, who argued Brown v. Board of Education and worked for equality under law.

name: Erik of Sweden
description: King Eric IX of Sweden (d. 1160), a just ruler who supported the Church and was killed during Mass. He is honoured as patron of Sweden.

name: Dunstan
description: Archbishop of Canterbury (c. 909-988), a craftsman, musician and reformer who renewed English monasteries and advised kings.

name: Alcuin of York
description: English scholar and deacon (c. 735-804) who led Charlemagne's palace school and promoted learning across Europe.

name: Helena, Mother of Constantine
description: Empress (c. 250-330) who made a pilgrimage to Jerusalem and built churches on the holy places. Lutherans and Anglicans remember her on May 21 or 22.

name: Helena and the Care of Holy Places
description: The Episcopal Church honours Helena for her care of the places where Christ lived and died.

name: John Wesley's Heart Warmed at Aldersgate
description: On May 24, 1738, John Wesley attended a meeting on Aldersgate Street in London and felt his heart 'strangely warmed'. He trusted Christ alone for salvation. The Lutheran calendar also remembers Copernicus and Euler on this day.

name: Bede the Venerable
description: English monk and historian (c. 673-735) who wrote the 'Ecclesiastical History of the English People'. Lutherans and Anglicans remember him on May 25.

name: Augustine of Canterbury
description: First archbishop of Canterbury (d. 605), sent by Gregory the Great in 597 to bring the Gospel to the Anglo-Saxons.

name: Mechthild of Magdeburg
description: German mystic (c. 1207-c. 1282) who became a Beguine and wrote 'The Flowing Light of the Godhead' about the soul's longing for God.

name: Juraj Tranovsky
description: Slovak Lutheran pastor and hymn writer (1592-1637), often called the 'Luther of the Slavs', whose hymnal 'Cithara Sanctorum' remains in use.

name: Joan of Arc
description: French peasant girl (c. 1412-1431) who, guided by what she believed were heavenly voices, helped lead France's army and was executed for heresy. Rehabilitated by the Church, she is honoured by many traditions.

name: Blandina and the Martyrs of Lyons
description: A slave woman who with many other Christians was tortured and killed in Lyons in 177. Her courage strengthened the other martyrs.

name: Hudson Taylor's Death and the Martyrs of Uganda
description: Hudson Taylor died on June 3, 1905, in China. The same date remembers the Ugandan martyrs killed in 1886 for refusing to renounce Christ.

name: John XXIII
description: Pope from 1958 to 1963 who called the Second Vatican Council and invited non-Catholic observers. Episcopalians and Lutherans remember him for his warmth and openness.

name: Chief Seattle
description: Leader of the Duwamish and Suquamish peoples (c. 1786-1866), baptised a Catholic, who sought peaceful relations with settlers and spoke for respect for the land.

name: Melania the Elder
description: Roman noblewoman (c. 342-410) who gave away her wealth, travelled to Egypt and Jerusalem and supported monks and exiles.

name: Columba, Aidan and Bede
description: Three saints of the British Isles: Columba (d. 597), who founded Iona; Aidan (d. 651), who evangelised Northumbria; and Bede (d. 735), the historian of the English Church.

name: Ephrem of Nisibis
description: Syrian deacon and poet (c. 306-373) who wrote hymns and commentaries and cared for the poor in time of famine. He is a Doctor of the Church in the West.

name: Barnabas, Apostle
description: A Levite from Cyprus called 'son of encouragement', who introduced Paul to the apostles and travelled with him on his first missionary journey.

name: Enmegahbowh
description: Ojibwe priest and missionary (c. 1810-1902), the first Native American ordained in the Episcopal Church, who protected settlers during the Dakota War of 1862.

name: The First Book of Common Prayer
description: Published in 1549 under Archbishop Cranmer, the Book of Common Prayer gave the English-speaking church worship in its own language.

name: Basil, Gregory and Macrina
description: The Cappadocian Fathers Basil the Great and Gregory of Nazianzus and Gregory of Nyssa, and their sister Macrina, taught the Trinity and a life of prayer and service.

name: Evelyn Underhill
description: English Anglican writer (1875-1941), author of 'Mysticism', and one of the most influential teachers of prayer and retreat in the twentieth century.

name: Joseph Butler
description: Anglican bishop and philosopher (1692-1752) whose 'Analogy of Religion' answered the deists of his time.

name: Marina the Monk
description: A young woman of the fifth century who lived in a men's monastery disguised as a monk named Marinos. Her patience under false accusation is remembered.

name: Bernard Mizeki
description: Mozambican catechist (c. 1861-1896) who taught the Shona people in Zimbabwe and was killed in the Mashonaland uprising. He is honoured as a martyr.

name: Charles Haddon Spurgeon's Birthday
description: Born on June 19, 1834, in Kelvedon, Essex. The 'Prince of Preachers' was converted at fifteen in a snowstorm hearing a simple sermon on Isaiah 45:22.

name: Onesimos Nesib
description: Ethiopian Oromo (c. 1856-1931), once a slave, who translated the Bible into Oromo and spread the Gospel among his people, supported by Swedish Lutheran missions.

name: Alban
description: First martyr of Britain (c. 304), a Roman soldier who sheltered a priest and took his place, and was beheaded. The city of Saint Albans is named for him.

name: Etheldreda of Ely
description: Anglo-Saxon queen and abbess (c. 636-679) who founded the monastery of Ely and lived in simplicity after leaving royal life.

name: The Augsburg Confession and Philip Melanchthon
description: On June 25, 1530, the Lutheran princes presented the Augsburg Confession to Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Augsburg, stating the faith of the Lutheran church.

name: Isabel Florence Hapgood
description: American translator and ecumenist (1851-1928) who translated Orthodox liturgical texts into English, building bridges between churches.

name: Cyril of Alexandria
description: Archbishop of Alexandria (c. 376-444) who defended the title Theotokos for Mary at the Council of Ephesus and wrote commentaries on Scripture.

name: Irenaeus of Lyons
description: Bishop of Lyons (c. 130-202) who wrote 'Against Heresies' and taught that God's plan unfolds in history. Lutherans and Anglicans honour him as a teacher of the faith.

name: Commemoration of Paul the Apostle
description: The Lutheran calendar completes the commemoration of Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles, whose letters make up much of the New Testament.

name: Catherine Winkworth and John Mason Neale
description: Hymn translators of the nineteenth century. Catherine Winkworth (1827-1878) rendered German chorales such as 'Now Thank We All Our God' into English; John Mason Neale (1818-1866) translated Greek and Latin hymns including 'O Come, O Come, Emmanuel'.

name: Moses the Black
description: Ethiopian former robber (c. 330-405) who became a monk in the Egyptian desert and a teacher of gentleness. He was killed by raiders while refusing to fight.

name: Thomas, Apostle
description: The apostle who doubted until he saw the risen Lord and then confessed 'my Lord and my God'. Tradition says he carried the Gospel to India.

name: Independence Day
description: The Episcopal Church marks the anniversary of the American Declaration of Independence with prayers for the nation and its people.
patronOf: The nation, those who pray for their country

name: Cyril and Methodius
description: Slovak Lutheran churches remember the brothers who brought the Gospel to the Slavs and gave them a written language in the ninth century.

name: Jan Hus
description: Czech priest and reformer (c. 1372-1415) who preached from the Bible in the people's language and was burned at the stake at Constance on July 6. The Moravian and other Protestant churches trace their roots to his witness.
patronOf: Czech lands, those who stand for truth

name: Priscilla and Aquila
description: The Episcopal Church remembers the couple who hosted Paul and taught Apollos, a model of shared ministry in marriage.

name: John Calvin's Birthday
description: John Calvin was born on July 10, 1509, at Noyon in France. Reformer of Geneva, his 'Institutes of the Christian Religion' shaped the Reformed churches around the world.

name: Benedict of Nursia
description: Italian abbot (c. 480-547) whose Rule shaped Western monasticism with its balance of prayer and work. Lutherans and Anglicans remember him on July 11.

name: Nathan Soderblom
description: Archbishop of Uppsala (1866-1931), a leader in the early ecumenical movement who convened the 1925 Stockholm conference on 'Life and Work' and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1930.

name: Argula von Grumbach
description: Bavarian noblewoman (c. 1492-1554) who wrote to the University of Ingolstadt in defence of a student persecuted for Lutheran views, becoming one of the first women writers of the Reformation.
patronOf: Women writers, those who speak for conscience

name: The Division of the Holy Apostles
description: A historic feast remembering the apostles' departure from Jerusalem to carry the Gospel to the ends of the earth.

name: Ruth the Moabite
description: The woman who said to Naomi 'where you go I will go', joined Israel, and became the great-grandmother of King David and an ancestor of Jesus.

name: Isaac Watts' Birthday and William White
description: Isaac Watts, the 'father of English hymnody', was born on July 17, 1674. William White (1748-1836) was the first Episcopal bishop of Pennsylvania and shaped the early Episcopal Church.

name: Macrina the Younger
description: Sister of Basil and Gregory of Nyssa (c. 327-379), who turned her family home into a community of prayer and taught her brothers.

name: Elijah the Prophet
description: The prophet who confronted the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel and heard the Lord in a 'still small voice'. He was taken up in a whirlwind and appeared with Christ at the Transfiguration.
patronOf: Prophets, those who pray in distress

name: Ezekiel the Prophet
description: Priest and prophet in exile in Babylon, who saw visions of God's glory and the valley of dry bones coming to life, a sign of hope for the exiles.
patronOf: Exiles, those who hope for renewal

name: Mary Magdalene
description: The woman healed by Jesus who stayed at the cross and was the first to see the risen Lord. The Church calls her 'apostle to the apostles'.
patronOf: Those who are healed, women disciples

name: Birgitta of Sweden
description: Swedish noblewoman and mystic (c. 1303-1373) who founded the Bridgettines, received visions and urged the Pope to return to Rome.

name: John Newton's Birthday and Thomas a Kempis
description: John Newton, former slave-ship captain and author of 'Amazing Grace', was born July 24, 1725. Thomas a Kempis (c. 1380-1471), author of 'The Imitation of Christ', is remembered on the same date in the Episcopal calendar.
patronOf: Those redeemed from sin, devotional writers

name: James, Apostle
description: James the son of Zebedee, called with his brother John from their fishing boat. He was the first of the twelve to die for the faith, killed by Herod Agrippa around 44.

name: Anne and Joachim, Parents of the Virgin Mary
description: The traditional names of the parents of Mary, remembered by Anglicans as a sign of the blessing of grandparents.

name: William Reed Huntington
description: Episcopal priest (1838-1909) whose 'Church Idea' helped shape the Chicago-Lambeth Quadrilateral, a basis for Christian unity.

name: Johann Sebastian Bach, Heinrich Schutz and George Frideric Handel
description: Three giants of church music. Bach (1685-1750) wrote cantatas, passions and the Mass in B minor; Schutz (1585-1672) was the father of German church music; Handel (1685-1759) wrote 'Messiah'.

name: William Wilberforce
description: English evangelical politician (1759-1833) who devoted his life to ending the slave trade. He heard the news that slavery would be abolished in the British Empire three days before his death on July 29.

name: Robert Barnes
description: English priest (c. 1495-1540) who studied at Cambridge, befriended Luther and was burned at Smithfield as a Reformation martyr.

name: Joseph of Arimathea
description: The rich member of the council who asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and buried him in his own new tomb. He is remembered for courage after hiding his faith.
patronOf: Those who give honour to the dead

name: Joseph of Arimathaea
description: The Episcopal Church honours Joseph, the disciple who offered his tomb for the burial of Jesus.

name: Joanna, Mary and Salome
description: Three of the women who came to the tomb on Easter morning with spices and were the first to hear the news of the resurrection.
patronOf: Women who witness to the resurrection

name: John Mason Neale
description: Anglican priest and hymn writer (1818-1866), warden of Sackville College, who translated many ancient hymns, including 'Good King Wenceslas' words and 'All glory, laud and honour'.

name: Dominic
description: Spanish priest (c. 1170-1221) who founded the Order of Preachers to teach the faith with preaching and study. Lutherans and Episcopalians honour him on August 8.

name: Edith Stein
description: German philosopher (1891-1942), a Jewish convert to Catholicism who became a Carmelite sister and was killed at Auschwitz.

name: Lawrence of Rome
description: Deacon of Rome who, when asked to hand over the treasure of the Church, brought the poor and said 'these are the Church's treasures'. He was martyred in 258.

name: Clare of Assisi
description: Italian abbess (1194-1253), friend of Francis, who founded the Poor Clares and lived in radical poverty at San Damiano.

name: Florence Nightingale
description: English nurse (1820-1910) who reformed military hospitals and founded the modern nursing profession, guided by her faith.

name: Florence Nightingale and Clara Maass
description: Lutherans remember Florence Nightingale and Clara Maass (1876-1901), an American nurse who volunteered for a yellow-fever experiment and died on August 24 after serving the sick.
patronOf: Nurses, those who serve the sick

name: Maximilian Kolbe and Kaj Munk
description: Maximilian Kolbe, a Polish Franciscan, gave his life in place of another prisoner at Auschwitz in 1941. Kaj Munk (1898-1944), a Danish Lutheran pastor and playwright, was killed by the Nazis for his preaching.

name: Mary, Mother of Our Lord
description: Lutherans and Anglicans honour Mary as the mother of the Lord, blessed among women, who said 'let it be to me according to your word'.

name: Isaac the Patriarch
description: The son of Abraham and Sarah, child of promise, who was spared at the altar and became the father of Jacob and Esau. His life is remembered for trust.
patronOf: Those who trust in God's promises

name: William Carey's Birthday and Johann Gerhard
description: William Carey, the 'father of modern missions', was born on August 17, 1761. Johann Gerhard (1582-1637) was a Lutheran theologian whose 'Sacred Meditations' were widely read.

name: Bernard of Clairvaux
description: French Cistercian abbot (1090-1153), preacher and hymn writer, author of 'Jesus, the Very Thought of Thee' and 'O Sacred Head, Now Wounded'. Lutherans remember him on August 19.

name: William Booth
description: English Methodist preacher (1829-1912) who founded the Salvation Army to reach the poor of London. He died on August 20.
patronOf: The poor, those who serve the homeless

name: Bartholomew, Apostle
description: One of the twelve apostles, usually identified with Nathanael, in whom Jesus saw 'no deceit'. Tradition says he preached in India and Armenia.

name: Louis IX of France
description: King of France (1214-1270), a just ruler who built the Sainte-Chapelle, cared for the poor and died on crusade in Tunis.

name: Simeon Bachos, the Ethiopian Eunuch
description: The treasurer of the queen of Ethiopia, baptised by Philip on the road to Gaza after reading Isaiah. Tradition says he carried the Gospel back to Africa.

name: Thomas Gallaudet and Henry Winter Syle
description: Two Episcopal priests (Gallaudet, d. 1902, and Syle, d. 1890) who ministered to the deaf community and founded churches for deaf congregations.
patronOf: The deaf, teachers of the deaf

name: Augustine of Hippo
description: Bishop of Hippo (354-430) who wrote 'Confessions' and 'The City of God'. His doctrine of grace deeply shaped Luther and Calvin and the Protestant Reformation.

name: The Beheading of John the Baptist
description: The forerunner who called Herod to repent was imprisoned and beheaded at the request of Herodias's daughter. His death is remembered as a witness to the truth.

name: Margaret Ward, Margaret Clitherow and Anne Line
description: Three English women martyred for sheltering priests during the persecution of Catholics under Elizabeth I.
patronOf: Women of courage, those who give shelter

name: John Bunyan
description: English Baptist preacher and writer (1628-1688), imprisoned for preaching without a licence, who wrote 'The Pilgrim's Progress' in jail. He died on August 31.

name: Joshua the Prophet
description: Moses' successor, who led Israel across the Jordan, and who proclaimed 'as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord'.
patronOf: Leaders, families who follow the Lord

name: N. F. S. Grundtvig
description: Danish pastor, poet and educator (1783-1872) who wrote over a thousand hymns and founded the folk high school movement, putting faith and learning in the service of ordinary people.

name: Phoebe the Deacon
description: The 'servant of the church at Cenchreae' whom Paul commended to the Romans, and who is thought to have carried his letter to Rome.

name: Moses the Lawgiver
description: The prophet who led Israel out of Egypt and received the law on Sinai, who spoke to God face to face 'as a man speaks with his friend'.

name: Katharina Zell
description: Reformer of Strasbourg (c. 1497-1562) who married a priest, defended clerical marriage in writing, cared for refugees and published hymns.

name: Hannah More
description: English writer and philanthropist (1745-1833) who founded schools for the poor in the Mendip Hills and wrote against the slave trade.

name: Kassiani the Hymnographer
description: Byzantine abbess and composer (c. 810-865) whose hymn for Holy Wednesday, sung to this day, tells of the woman who anointed Christ's feet.

name: Peter Claver
description: Spanish Jesuit (1580-1654) who ministered to enslaved Africans arriving at Cartagena and called himself 'the slave of the slaves forever'.

name: Alexander Crummell
description: African American Episcopal priest (1819-1898), scholar and missionary in Liberia, who founded the American Negro Academy and argued for the dignity of the Black church.

name: John Henry Hobart
description: Episcopal bishop of New York (1775-1830), a leader in the revival of the Church after the American Revolution.

name: John Chrysostom
description: Archbishop of Constantinople (c. 347-407) whose preaching earned him the name 'golden-mouthed'. He urged care for the poor and was exiled by the court.

name: Holy Cross Day
description: The Church lifts up the cross as the sign of salvation and recalls the finding of the True Cross in Jerusalem. 'We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy cross you have redeemed the world'.

name: Catherine of Genoa
description: Italian mystic and nurse (1447-1510) who worked in a hospital in Genoa and wrote about purgatory and the love of God.

name: Cyprian of Carthage
description: Bishop of Carthage (c. 200-258) who held the Church together through plague and persecution, writing 'On the Unity of the Church' and dying a martyr.

name: Hildegard of Bingen
description: German abbess (1098-1179), composer, writer, healer and visionary who wrote 'Scivias', sacred music and works on natural medicine.

name: Dag Hammarskjold
description: Swedish diplomat (1905-1961), Secretary-General of the United Nations, whose private journal 'Markings' shows a deep Christian faith. He died in a plane crash on a peace mission.

name: Theodore of Tarsus
description: Greek monk (c. 602-690) appointed archbishop of Canterbury at the age of 66, who organised the English Church and founded schools.

name: John Coleridge Patteson and Companions
description: Anglican bishop of Melanesia (1827-1871) killed on the island of Nukapu, together with others, after founding a school for islanders.

name: Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist
description: The tax collector called from his booth by Jesus, who wrote the Gospel that begins the New Testament.
patronOf: Evangelists, those who change their lives

name: Jonah the Prophet
description: The prophet who ran from God's call to Nineveh, was swallowed by a great fish and then preached repentance to a city that turned to the Lord.
patronOf: Those who run from God's call

name: Thecla of Iconium
description: Early Christian woman converted by Saint Paul's preaching, venerated as the first woman martyr (c. 70) in the 'Acts of Paul and Thecla'.

name: Anna Alexander
description: African American Episcopal deaconess (1865-1947) who founded and led a church and school for Black children in Georgia.

name: The Peace of Augsburg
description: Concluded on September 25, 1555, it gave Lutheran princes the right to practise their faith in the Holy Roman Empire, ending decades of conflict.

name: Lancelot Andrewes
description: Anglican bishop (1555-1626) and a translator of the King James Bible, whose 'Private Prayers' are widely loved.

name: Euphrosyne of Alexandria
description: A young woman of the fifth century who disguised herself as a monk named Smaragdus and spent thirty-eight years in a monastery.

name: Paula and Eustochium
description: Roman mother (347-404) and daughter who followed Jerome to Bethlehem, founded monasteries and helped with his Bible translation.

name: Michael and All Angels
description: The Church honours the archangel Michael and all the angels who serve God and guard his people. 'Bless the Lord, O you his angels, you mighty ones who do his word'.

name: Jerome
description: Latin scholar (c. 347-420) who translated the Bible into Latin, the Vulgate, and wrote commentaries. Lutherans and Anglicans honour him as a translator of Scripture.

name: Remigius of Rheims
description: Bishop of Reims (c. 437-533) who baptised Clovis, king of the Franks, and thereby helped bring the Frankish people into the Church.

name: John R. Mott
description: American Methodist layman (1865-1955) who helped found the World Student Christian Federation and led the ecumenical movement. He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1946.

name: Francis of Assisi
description: Italian friar (c. 1181-1226) who embraced poverty, preached to the birds and received the stigmata. The Lutheran and Anglican calendars honour him as a renewer of the Church.

name: Henry Melchior Muhlenberg
description: German-born pastor (1711-1787), 'patriarch of the Lutheran Church in America', who organised congregations in Pennsylvania and across the colonies.

name: Abraham the Patriarch
description: The father of all who believe, who left his homeland at God's call and trusted God's promise of descendants as numerous as the stars.
patronOf: Those who step out in faith

name: Vida Dutton Scudder
description: American Episcopal educator and social reformer (1861-1954), professor at Wellesley, who helped found the Church League for Industrial Democracy.

name: Philip the Evangelist
description: One of the seven deacons of the Jerusalem church, who preached in Samaria and baptised the Ethiopian official, and whose four daughters prophesied.

name: Edith Cavell
description: English nurse (1865-1915) who helped hundreds of Allied soldiers escape from German-occupied Belgium and was executed on October 12. Her last words: 'Patriotism is not enough'.

name: Samuel Schereschewsky
description: Lithuanian-born Jewish convert (1831-1906) who became Episcopal bishop of Shanghai and translated the Bible into Chinese despite paralysis.

name: Teresa of Avila
description: Spanish Carmelite reformer (1515-1582) and mystic who wrote 'The Interior Castle' and taught that prayer is 'a close sharing between friends'.

name: Hugh Latimer, Nicholas Ridley and Thomas Cranmer
description: Three Anglican bishops burned under Queen Mary I at Oxford: Latimer and Ridley on October 16, 1555, Cranmer in 1556. Latimer said 'we shall this day light such a candle'.

name: Ignatius of Antioch
description: Bishop of Antioch martyred in Rome around 115. On his way he wrote letters to the churches, urging unity and love.

name: Luke, Evangelist
description: The physician and companion of Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles, with its special care for the poor, women and the outcast.

name: Henry Martyn
description: Anglican priest and missionary (1781-1812) who translated the New Testament into Urdu and Persian and died at the age of 31 in Tokat, Turkey.

name: Cornelius the Centurion
description: The Roman officer of Caesarea whose household was the first Gentile family baptised by Peter, a sign that the Gospel was for all peoples.

name: James of Jerusalem
description: Brother of the Lord and first bishop of Jerusalem, called 'the Just', who presided at the council of Jerusalem and wrote the letter of James.

name: Tabitha (Dorcas) of Joppa
description: The disciple 'full of good works and acts of charity' whom Peter raised from the dead at Joppa. The widows showed him the garments she had made.
patronOf: Seamstresses, those who serve the poor

name: Philipp Nicolai, Johann Heermann and Paul Gerhardt
description: Three German Lutheran hymn writers of the seventeenth century: Nicolai ('Wake, Awake'), Heermann ('Ah, Holy Jesus') and Gerhardt ('O Sacred Head, Now Wounded').

name: Simon and Jude, Apostles
description: Two of the twelve apostles, Simon the Zealot and Jude Thaddaeus. Tradition says they preached together in Persia and were martyred.

name: James Hannington and Companions
description: Anglican bishop of Eastern Equatorial Africa (1847-1885) killed with his companions in Uganda on the orders of King Mwanga.

name: Maryam of Qidun
description: A young woman of Syria who devoted herself to prayer in the fourth century and cared for her uncle Abraham of Qidun.

name: Reformation Day
description: On October 31, 1517, Martin Luther posted his Ninety-Five Theses on the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg, beginning the Protestant Reformation. 'The just shall live by faith'.

name: All Souls
description: The Episcopal Church remembers all the faithful departed, trusting them to the mercy of God. 'Rest eternal grant them, O Lord, and let light perpetual shine upon them'.

name: Richard Hooker
description: English Anglican priest and theologian (1554-1600), whose 'Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity' defended the Church of England and taught the balance of Scripture, tradition and reason.

name: Adeline Blanchard Tyler and Companions
description: Missionaries remembered by the Episcopal Church for their work in Africa and the Philippines.

name: William Temple
description: Archbishop of Canterbury (1881-1944), a theologian and social reformer who laid foundations for the British welfare state and the World Council of Churches.

name: Willibrord, Missionaries to the Netherlands
description: Northumbrian bishop (658-739) who became the 'apostle of the Frisians'. The Lutheran calendar also remembers Heyer, Ziegenbalg and Nommensen, missionaries to India and Indonesia.

name: Johann von Staupitz
description: Luther's superior and confessor (c. 1460-1524), who taught him that true repentance begins with the love of God and helped lead him to the Scriptures.

name: Martin Chemnitz and the Mystics of England
description: Martin Chemnitz (1522-1586) was a Lutheran theologian who helped write the Formula of Concord. The Episcopal Church recalls Richard Rolle, Walter Hilton and Margery Kempe, English mystics.

name: Martin Luther's Birthday
description: Martin Luther was born on November 10, 1483, in Eisleben. He died in the same town in 1546. The Church remembers his birth and his work as a teacher of Scripture and grace.

name: Martin of Tours
description: Roman soldier turned bishop (c. 316-397) who famously shared his cloak with a beggar. Lutherans honour him, and Luther himself was baptised on his feast.

name: Charles Simeon
description: Anglican priest (1759-1836) who served Holy Trinity, Cambridge, for 54 years, trained many young clergy and supported missionary societies.

name: Justinian and the Consecration of Samuel Seabury
description: The Lutheran calendar remembers Emperor Justinian (d. 565), who built Hagia Sophia and codified Roman law. The Episcopal Church marks the 1784 consecration of Samuel Seabury as first American bishop.

name: Herman of Alaska
description: Russian Orthodox monk (c. 1756-1837) who served the Aleut people on Spruce Island and protected them from abuse.

name: Margaret of Scotland
description: Anglo-Saxon princess and Queen of Scotland (c. 1045-1093) who supported church reform and cared for orphans and the poor.

name: Elisabeth of Hungary
description: Hungarian princess (1207-1231) who cared for the poor and the sick, building hospitals and giving away her goods. The ELCA remembers her on November 17.

name: Hilda of Whitby
description: English abbess (614-680) who hosted the Synod of Whitby and encouraged the poet Caedmon, the first English Christian poet.

name: Elizabeth of Hungary
description: Princess and charity worker who gave bread to the poor and cared for lepers. Her feast is on November 17 or 19 in various calendars.

name: Edmund, King and Martyr
description: King of East Anglia (c. 841-870) killed by Danish invaders after refusing to renounce Christ.

name: Gertrude the Great and Mechthilde of Hackeborn
description: German nuns and mystics of the monastery of Helfta, who wrote about the love of Christ and gave great importance to the Scriptures and the liturgy.

name: C. S. Lewis
description: Oxford and Cambridge scholar and apologist (1898-1963), author of 'Mere Christianity', 'The Screwtape Letters' and 'The Chronicles of Narnia'. He died on November 22.

name: Clement of Rome
description: Bishop of Rome around 92-101, who wrote a letter to Corinth urging peace and order. Lutherans and Episcopalians remember him on November 23.

name: John Knox, Justus Falckner and Jehu Jones
description: John Knox (c. 1514-1572) led the Scottish Reformation and died on November 24. Lutherans remember Justus Falckner, Jehu Jones and William Passavant, American pastors.

name: Isaac Watts
description: English Congregational minister (1674-1748), the 'father of English hymnody', author of 'Joy to the World' and 'When I Survey the Wondrous Cross'.

name: Sojourner Truth
description: Sojourner Truth (c. 1797-1883), a freed slave and preacher, spoke for the equality of women and the end of slavery. She died on November 26.

name: Kamehameha IV and Queen Emma of Hawaii
description: The Hawaiian king and queen (1834-1863; 1836-1885) who founded the Anglican Church in Hawaii and the Queen's Hospital.

name: Noah the Patriarch
description: The righteous man who built the ark at God's command and survived the flood with his family. God set the rainbow as a sign of his covenant.
patronOf: Those who obey God in the face of ridicule

name: Andrew, Apostle
description: The fisherman who followed Jesus first and brought his brother Peter to him. Andrew is honoured as patron of Scotland, Greece and Russia.

name: Charles de Foucauld
description: French hermit (1858-1916) who lived among the Tuareg in the Sahara, a witness of quiet presence. He was killed on December 1.
patronOf: Hermits, those who live among strangers

name: Martyrs of El Salvador
description: Four American women missionaries, Maura Clarke, Ita Ford, Dorothy Kazel and Jean Donovan, killed by soldiers in El Salvador on December 2, 1980.

name: Francis Xavier
description: Spanish Jesuit missionary (1506-1552) who carried the Gospel to India, Southeast Asia and Japan. He died on Sancian Island off China on December 3.

name: John of Damascus
description: Syrian monk and theologian (c. 675-749) who defended icons and wrote hymns still sung at Easter, including 'The Day of Resurrection'.

name: Clement of Alexandria
description: Greek Christian teacher (c. 150-215) who headed the catechetical school of Alexandria and argued that philosophy prepares for Christ.

name: Nicholas of Myra
description: Bishop of Myra in Asia Minor (d. c. 342) known for secret gifts to the poor. The figure of Santa Claus grew from his legend.
patronOf: Children, sailors, those who give in secret

name: Ambrose of Milan
description: Bishop of Milan (c. 339-397) who baptised Augustine, wrote hymns and stood against the emperor to defend the Church's freedom.

name: Nicholas Ferrar
description: English Anglican deacon (1593-1637) who founded a household community at Little Gidding devoted to prayer and charity.
patronOf: Deacons, those who live in community

name: Frederick Howden Jr.
description: Episcopal priest and chaplain (1900-1942) who ministered to servicemen in World War II and was killed during the invasion of North Africa.

name: Francis de Sales and Jane de Chantal
description: Savoyard bishop (1567-1622) and widowed baroness (1572-1641) who founded the Visitation Sisters. Francis wrote 'Introduction to the Devout Life', a classic for lay Christians.

name: Lucy of Syracuse
description: Sicilian virgin and martyr (d. 304) whose name means 'light'. In Sweden and Norway Lucy's Day, with its processions of candles, brightens the dark days of winter.

name: John of the Cross
description: Spanish Carmelite mystic (1542-1591), co-reformer of the Carmelites, who wrote 'The Dark Night of the Soul' and the 'Spiritual Canticle'.

name: Nino of Georgia
description: A slave woman of the fourth century (c. 296-332) who brought the Gospel to Georgia after healing the queen. She is honoured as the 'enlightener of Georgia'.

name: Daniel and the Three Young Men
description: Daniel and his friends Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, who stayed faithful in Babylon and trusted God in the lions' den and the fiery furnace.
patronOf: Those who remain faithful in exile

name: Charles Wesley's Birthday
description: Charles Wesley was born on December 18, 1707, and wrote some six thousand hymns, including 'Hark! The Herald Angels Sing', 'Love Divine' and 'And Can It Be'.

name: Adam and Eve
description: The first man and woman, created in God's image, whose fall and promise of redemption frame the Bible's story of salvation.

name: Katharina von Bora Luther
description: Former nun (1499-1552) who married Martin Luther, ran the household and farm of the Black Cloister and became a model of Reformation marriage and hospitality.

name: Thomas, Apostle
description: The apostle who touched the wounds of Christ and said 'my Lord and my God'. His feast is kept on December 21 by the Lutheran and Episcopal calendars.

name: D. L. Moody's Death
description: Dwight L. Moody (1837-1899), shoe salesman turned evangelist, preached to millions in America and Britain and founded schools and the Moody Bible Institute. He died on December 22.

name: Vigil of the Nativity
description: On Christmas Eve the Church keeps vigil, reading the prophecies and the Gospel of the birth of Jesus, and prepares to welcome the light of Christ.

name: Stephen, Deacon and Martyr
description: The first Christian martyr, a deacon who served the poor and was stoned in Jerusalem as he prayed 'Lord, do not hold this sin against them'.

name: John, Apostle and Evangelist
description: The beloved disciple who rested at the Last Supper on the breast of the Lord. Tradition says he wrote the fourth Gospel, three letters and the Book of Revelation.

name: David the King
description: The shepherd boy who became king of Israel, the 'sweet psalmist' and ancestor of Jesus. The Lutheran calendar remembers him in the days after Christmas.

name: John Wycliffe
description: English priest and scholar (c. 1328-1384), called the 'Morning Star of the Reformation', who supervised the first complete English translation of the Bible. He died on December 31.

name: Henry Purcell
description: English composer (c. 1659-1695), organist of Westminster Abbey, who wrote anthems, odes and theatre music for the Anglican church and court. He died on November 21, 1695, and is buried near the Abbey organ.

name: John Milton
description: English poet (born December 9, 1608) who wrote 'Paradise Lost', a great epic of the Fall and redemption, and 'Paradise Regained'. He continued to compose after losing his sight.
patronOf: Poets, writers, those who persevere through blindness

name: Meryem, Tanrı'nın Anası
description: Kilise yıla, 431'de Efes'te onaylanan en eski Meryem unvanıyla, Theotokos ('Tanrı'yı doğuran') ile başlar. Oğlu gerçekten Tanrı olduğu için Meryem gerçekten Tanrı'nın Anası'dır.

name: İsa'nın Kutsal Adı
description: 'Tanrı kurtarır' anlamına gelen İsa adına duyulan bağlılık bayramı. Sienalı Aziz Bernardino ve Fransiskenler, Kutsal Ad'ı sevgi ve saygıyla anma geleneğini yaydı.

name: Aziz John Neumann
description: Bohemya doğumlu Redemptorist (1811-1860); Philadelphia piskoposu oldu. Amerika Birleşik Devletleri'nde ilk Katolik piskoposluk okul sistemini kurdu ve göçmenlere birkaç dilde hizmet etti.

name: Aziz Raymond of Penyafort
description: İspanyol Dominikan kilise hukukçusu (yaklaşık 1175-1275). Kilise kararlarını tek bir derlemede topladı ve Aziz Peter Nolasco'nun tutsakları kurtarmasına yardım etti. İtirafta gösterdiği yumuşaklıkla tanınırdı.

name: Noricumlu Aziz Severinus
description: Tuna boyunda yaşayan beşinci yüzyıl keşişi ve misyoneri. Roma yönetiminin çöküşü sırasında açları doyurdu, tutsakları kurtardı, halka teselli verdi. Romalılar da barbarlar da ona güvendi.

name: Canterbury'li Aziz Adrian
